label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Across all three psychological distress measures, this group scores notably higher than typical respondents, with anxiety symptoms being the most pronounced (mean GAD-7 item score of 2.27). The co-occurrence of heavy social-media engagement and heightened emotional distress is a defining characteristic of this cluster.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness as measured by UCLA-8 (mean item score ~1.78)
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology on PHQ-9 (mean item score ~1.81)
Highest anxiety levels among profiles on GAD-7 (mean item score ~2.27)
Pattern of co-occurring psychological distress across loneliness, depression, and anxiety dimensions
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of digital overuse and significant emotional vulnerability

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report lower loneliness, lower depressive symptoms, and lower anxiety compared to other profiles. They engage in relatively light daily social-media use, averaging roughly 2.8 hours per day (within the 1–3 hour bracket). Their psychological well-being indicators are consistently favorable, with notably low scores on loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78), depression (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27), and anxiety (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03).
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use approximately 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media consumption averaging around 2.8 hours
Consistently low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27)
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03)
Pattern of moderate and bounded digital engagement

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who report elevated loneliness despite relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. They spend nearly five hours per day on social media, suggesting that heavy platform use may coexist with social disconnection rather than acute psychological distress. Their loneliness scores stand out as the defining feature, while clinical mood and anxiety indicators remain comparatively subdued.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate perceived social isolation
Below-average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90) suggesting low clinical depression burden
Below-average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85) indicating limited generalized anxiety
Heavy daily social-media use averaging approximately 4.9 hours
Possible pattern of using social media as a substitute for in-person social connection without it alleviating loneliness
tone: Reflective and socially seeking; outwardly functional yet quietly disconnected

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents a relatively large group (n = 217) of male respondents with graduate-level education who report low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social-media use is light, averaging roughly 1.6 hours per day (self-reported range of 1–3 hours). Across all three psychological well-being scales, their scores fall well below clinical concern thresholds, suggesting generally positive mental health and social connectedness.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media use averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.22, well below scale midpoint)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.82)
Low anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.90)
Pattern consistent with balanced, non-excessive digital engagement
